results.title: Computational Optical Imaging and Artificial Intelligence in ...
results.content: Our approach enables real-time, high-resolution 3D reconstruction across large imaging volumes. Our model produced virtually stained images closely resembling corresponding high-resolution bright-field images of H&E-stained tissue sections, demonstrating improvements of ~4–5-fold in spatial resolution relative to the original label-free microscopy inputs. AccessPath integrates an end-to-end optimized compact optical design, deep UV surface excitation, and a sensor array into a 6×8 array-microscopy platform for high-throughput cellular-resolution imaging of intact resected tissue without histologic sectioning. SWIR imaging (1000-1700 nm) enables deep tissue penetration through reduced scattering, while light-field techniques provide efficient 3D snapshot capabilities. In this contribution, we present a multi-modal optical 3D imaging technique for specular surface reconstruction, which is further integrated into a physics-informed deep learning framework to enhance robustness and generalizability. In this study, we introduce a fast and reliable imaging and analysis pipeline that combines a novel multiplane 2.5D microscopy technique with a deep learning-based cell-level classifier.
